sentences.text: This claim petition claimed by the claimants seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ for the death of Sri. Narayanaswamy S/o Munidasappa, in the accident occurred on 15.09.2021.
SCCH - 7 2.

It is the case of the petitioners that on 15.09.2021 at about 800 p.m., when the deceased Narayanaswamy was proceeding in Tractor and Tailor bearing registration No.KA44T1113 and KA40T7254 in Akkimangala Village, near T. Hosahalli Gate, Gudappa Bangalore Road, at that time driver of Milk Tanker bearing registration No.KA01AL8683 drove the same in rash and negligent manner without observing the traffic rules and dashed to the Tractor and Trailer from behind and due to impact deceased fell down and tractor wheel ran over the head of Narayanswamy and he died on spot.
As on the date of the accident the deceased Narayanswamy was aged about 48 years and he was working as Coolie  Labour and earning Rs.30,000/ p.m.
Due to suddenly and untimely death of the Narayanaswamy they lost their earning member of their family and they are undergoing great mental shock, agony and financial loss.
The respondents are jointly and SCCH - 7 severally liable to pay compensation to them.
Hence they prayed to allow the petition.

3. In response to the notice issued by this Tribunal, the respondent No.1 to 3 have appeared through their counsel and respondent No.2 has not filed written statement and respondent No.1 and 3 filed the written statement.
4. The respondent No.1 - owner of the tanker denied the entire contentions of the petitioner.
The respondent No.1 contended that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the tractor and trailer by its driver.
The petitioners have suppressed the real facts and has come up with this baseless application seeking for the award of the compensation.

Even as per the complaint lodged by the Munilakshmamma to the Cintamani Rural Police it is alleged that the deceased was sitting on the fender of the tractor, the driver of the tractor was driving SCCH - 7 the said tractor and trailer in a rash and negligent manner, as a result, the deceased who was sitting on the engine or fender of the tractor fell down and the wheel of the tractor ran over the him and there is a negligence on the part of the driver of the tanker.
The driver of the tractor and trailer allowing of the deceased to sit on the engine of the tractor itself
shows the negligence on the part of the driver of the tractor which is violation of the provisions of the motor vehicle as such there are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, on all these grounds, the respondent No.1 has prayed for dismissal of claim petition.
5. The respondent No.3  insurer of the tractor and trailer bearing No.KA44T1113 and KA40 T7254
denied the entire contentions of the petitioner.

Further the respondent No.3 admitted that they have issued the Insurance Policy to the Tractor and Trailer bearing registration No.KA44T 1113 and KA40T7254 and their liability is subjected to SCCH - 7 terms and conditions of the policy.

The respondent No.3 contended that as on the date of the accident the driver of Tractor and Trailer was not having valid and effective driving licence, as such it is violation of terms and Munivenkatamma vs R. Narayanaswamy on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122510435/
3 conditions of the policy as such there are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, on all these grounds, the respondent No.2 has prayed for dismissal of claim petition.
6. On the basis of above pleadings following Issues were framed.
:: I S S U E S ::

(1) Whether the Petitioners proves that deceased Sri. Narayanaswamy S/o Munidasappa sustained injuries due to the rash and negligent act of driving of Tanker bearing registration No.KA01 SCCH - 7 AL8683 dated 15.09.2021 at about 8.00 p.m., and succumbed to injuries?
(2) Whether the Petitioners proves the age and earnings of the deceased as stated in the claim petition?
(3) Whether the petitioners prove that they are legal heirs of deceased Narayanaswamy S/o Munidasappa?

(4) Whether petitioners are entitled for  compensation? If so, what is the  quantum? from whom?
 (5) What order or award?
7.

As per the case of the petitioners that the deceased Narayanswamy was proceeding on the Tractor and Trailer when the Tractor and Trailer was proceeding near T. Hosahalli Gate, Kadapa - Bengaluru road the driver of the Tractor and Trailer driving the same in slowly on the left side of the road at that time the driver of the Tanker bearing registration No.KA01AL8383 drove the same in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the Tractor and Trailer from behind due to the force of the accident Narayanaswamy fell down from the Tractor and Tractor tyre ran over him and died due to the injuries sustained in the accident.

The PW.1 is the wife of the deceased and from the evidence of PW.1 it is clear that she has not seen this accident and he deposed that at the time of accident her husband was traveling on the Tractor and Trailer and Tanker dashed to the Trailer and her husband fell down and struck under the wheel of the Tractor and died due to SCCH - 7 the injuries sustained in the accident.

The RW.2 is the driver of the Tractor and Trailer and he is an eye witness and he deposed that in the Tractor himself and Narayanaswamy were proceeding near road hump he was driving the Tractor and Trailer slowly at that time from the back side the Tanker came and dashed to the Trailer at that time the Narayanaswamy who was sitting on the engine fell down and tractor wheel ran over the Narayanswamy due to which Narayanaswamy died.
From the evidence of RW.2 it is clear that the deceased was sitting on the mudguard of the engine and this witness was driving the Tractor and trailer.
By perusing the evidence of this witness and spot sketch marked as per Ex.P.4 they clear that near the road hump this accident was took place.
Further it goes to shows that the Tractor was crossing the road hump at that time from the back side the Tanker came and dashed to the Trailer due to which this accident was SCCH - 7 took place.
The driver of the Tanker is examined as RW.4 by respondent No.1 and he is also an eye witness.

From the evidence of RW.4 it goes to shows that when the driver of the Tractor and Trailer was suddenly stopped the Tractor and Trailer on the road hump without giving any sign or signal as such as his Tanker was coming from the back side of his Tractor and Trailer and he lost control over the Tanker and dashed to the Trailer.

It shows that at the road hump when the Tractor was slow down at that time from the back side Munivenkatamma vs R. Narayanaswamy on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122510435/
7 Tanker which was coming dashed to the Trailer.
The Tractor engine is meant for only attaching the trailer and part from the driver there is no any other provision for any other person to travel in the engine.
It shows that the driver of the Tractor was permitted the deceased to travel in the Tractor by sitting on the mudguard.

Further it is an admitted fact that from the back side of the Tractor and Trailer the Milk Tanker was SCCH - 7 coming and it is also clear from the evidence of RW.2, RW.4 and Ex.P.4 this accident was took place at road hump at 8 00 p.m.
When the Tractor and Trailer was proceeding in front of the Tanker at the night hours it is not visible for the Tanker driver at a some distance there is a road hump.

At the time of the accident in front of the tanker the Tractor and Trailer was proceeding and the driver of the Tractor and Trailer at the road hump slow down his vehicle or stopped his vehicle without giving any sign or signal at that time the tanker was coming from the back side
the tractor and trailer and Tanker driver was not able to control his vehicle and dashed to the Trailer.

If the driver of the Tractor and Trailer was cautious and he was given signal or sign and slow down his vehicle at the road hump the driver of the Tanker could have control his vehicle and this accident would have avoided but from the evidence of both parties it goes to shows that the driver of the Tractor and SCCH - 7 Trailer was negligent in crossing the road hump suddenly slow down and the Tractor and Trailer without giving any sign or signal at the same time the Tanker was came from the back side of the Tractor and Trailer and the driver was driving the tanker in high speed, rash and negligent manner and he has not maintained proper distance in between his Tanker and the Tractor and Trailer and suddenly drove the same and dashed to the Tralier due to which the deceased Narayanaswamy who was sitting on the mudguard and driver of the tractor and trailer were fell down due to the force of the accident and tractor wheel ran over the head of Narayanaswamy due to which he sustained grievous injuries.

Further it is also clear from the police records that due to the force of the dashing trailer by the Tanker the driver of the tractor and trailer went towards extreme left side of the road and dashed to the road side shop and caused damages to the shop.

It shows that in SCCH - 7 this accident due to the force of the dashing the trailer by the Milk Tanker the person who was traveling in the Tractor was fell down and one of the passenger died due to the injuries sustained in the accident and Tractor also dashed one shop on the left side of the road and caused damages.
Hence it is clear that in this accident there is negligence of the driver of the Tractor and Trailer and also driver of the Tanker and they are equally contributed in this accident.
Hence I am of the considered view that the driver of the Tractor and Trailer is contributed his negligence to an extent of 50% and driver of the Tanker contributed his negligence to an extent of 50%.
Hence, I answered the Issue No.1 Partly in the affirmative.
21. Issue No.2: The petitioners are contended that as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged about 48 years and he was doing Coolie Labour and earning Rs.30,000/ SCCH - 7 p.m.
The petitioners relied on the Postmortem Report marked as per Ex.P.7 wherein the age of the deceased is shown as 48 years.
Hence the age of the deceased is considered as 48 years.
22. Further the petitioner contended that the deceased was doing Coolie Labour and earning Rs.30,000/ p.m.
In support of this contention the petitioners are not produced any documents to prove that the deceased was earning Rs.30,000/ per month.
Under such circumstances by perusing the age, cost of leaving at the relevant time the notional income of the deceased is considered at Rs.15,000/ p.m.
Hence, I answered the Issue No.2 Partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.3:
The petitioners are contended that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Narayanaswamy.
In support of this contention the petitioners are produced Ration Card SCCH - 7 as per Ex.P.9 and Adhar Cards of the petitioners as per Ex.P.10 to Ex.P.12.
By perusing these documents they goes to shows that the petitioner No.1 is the mother, petitioner No.2 is the wife and petitioners No.3 to 5 are the children of the deceased Narayanaswamy.
To rebut the case of the petitioner nothing worth is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioners.

Hence by looking to the contention of the petitioner and oral and documentary evidence adduced by the petitioners I am of the considered view that the petitioners No.1 to 5 are the legal heirs of the deceased Narayanaswamy.
Hence, I answered the Issue No.3 in the affirmative.
24. Issue No.4:
From the evidence of PW.1 it is clear that petitioner No.1 is the mother, petitioner No.2 is the wife and petitioner No.3 to 5 are the major daughters of the deceased.
They contended that they are depending on the SCCH - 7 income of the deceased.
By perusing the petition averments and evidence of PW.1 it is clear that all the petitioners are majors and they are having independent source of income.

In the authority reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356 in between National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Birender and Others wherein it is held that it is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased having right to apply for compensation.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Birender and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having said that it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact that whether they are fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit their claim towards conventional head only.
From the above said authority it is clear that even though the major, married and earning sons of the deceased being the legal representatives have right to apply compensation.
SCCH - 7
Further it is also clear from the above said authority that the concerned legal representatives were fully dependent of the deceased and not to limit claim towards conventional head only.
Hence by relying on the above said authority I am of he considered view that the petitioners are the dependents of the deceased.
Hence the petitioners No.1 to 5 are considered as dependents of the deceased.
25. As per Sarla Varma case 1/4th of the income is to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased.
Further as per Sarla Varma case multiplier 13 is applicable in the present case on hand.

Further as per authority reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs., Pranay Sethi 25% is added towards future prospectus of the deceased as he was aged about 48 years.

Hence, out of Rs.15,000/, if 1/4 th is deducted i.e. Rs.3,750/ it comes to Rs.11,250/
and to SCCH - 7 Rs.11,250/, if 25% is added i.e., Rs.2,812/ it comes to Rs.14,062/.

Hence,
monthly income comes to Rs.14,062/ and loss of dependency works out to Rs.21,93,672/
(Rs.14,062/ X 12 X 13).
The petitioner No.1 is the mother she lost her son, petitioner No.2 is the wife has lost her husband and petitioners No.3 to 5 are the children they lost their father.

Hence as per the authority reported in (2018) 18 Supreme Court Cases 130 in between Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs., Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and Others the petitioners No.1 is entitled for filial consortium of Rs.40,000/, petitioner No.2 is entitled for spousal consortium of Rs.40,000/ and petitioners No 3 to 5 are entitled for parental consortium of Rs.40,000/ each.

Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under following heads;

26.

While answering the issue No.1 this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the Tractor and Trailor bearing registration No.KA44T1113 and KA40T7254 and so also due to the negligence of the driver of the Milk Tanker bearing registration No.KA01AL8683.

The respondent No.3 has admitted that as on the date of the accident the Tractor and Trailer bearing registration No.KA44T1113 and KA40T 7254 was insured by them, but the tractoir and trailer was SCCH - 7 not having FC as such it is violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.
In support of this contention the respondent No.3 got examined the FDA of Chikkabllapur RTO as RW.1.
In his examination in chief he deposed that on 15.09.2021 the tractor No.KA44T1113 was not having FC.
As on 15.09.2021 due to Carona Lock dwon the offices are closed and renewal of the FC was extended up to 30.09.2021
as such it was considered as the tractor was having FC as on the date of the accident.
He has produced the authorisation letter as per Ex.R1, B register extract of the tractor No. KA44T1113 and traler No.KA40T2254 as per Ex.R2 and 3.
from the evidence of RW.1 it is clear that as on the date of the accident the tractor bearing No.KA44T1113 was having FC.
Hence the contention of the respondent No.3 is not acceptable one.
27. As on the date of the accident the policy issued to the tractor No. KA44T1113 and trailer No.KA40T2254 was SCCH - 7 in force and there is not violation of the terms and conditions of the policy
, as such the respondent No.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

As this accident is occurred due to the negligence of the driver Tractor and Tailor bearing registration No.KA44T1113 and KA40T7254 and so also due to the negligence of the driver of the Milk Tanker bearing registration No.KA01AL8683 and the drivers of both vehicles are equally contributed for this accident and there is contributory negligence in between the drivers of the above said vehicles.

Hence I am of the considered view that the respondent No.1 being the owner Milk Tanker bearing registration No.KA01AL8683 is liable to pay 50% of the compensation amount and respondent No.2 being the owner of the Tractor and Tailor bearing registration No.KA 44T1113 and KA40T7254 and Respondent No.3 being the insurer of the said Tractor and Trailer are jointly and SCCH - 7 severally liable to pay 50% of the compensation amount to the petitioners along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition.
Hence I answered the Issue No.3 partly in the Affirmative.

opennyai_summary.facts:
As on the date of the accident the deceased Narayanswamy was aged about 48 years and he was working as Coolie  Labour and earning Rs.30,000/ p.m.
Due to suddenly and untimely death of the Narayanaswamy they lost their earning member of their family and they are undergoing great mental shock, agony and financial loss.
The respondents are jointly and SCCH - 7 severally liable to pay compensation to them.
Hence they prayed to allow the petition.
3. In response to the notice issued by this Tribunal, the respondent No.1 to 3 have appeared through their counsel and respondent No.2 has not filed written statement and respondent No.1 and 3 filed the written statement.
4. The respondent No.1 - owner of the tanker denied the entire contentions of the petitioner.
The respondent No.1 contended that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the tractor and trailer by its driver.
Even as per the complaint lodged by the Munilakshmamma to the Cintamani Rural Police it is alleged that the deceased was sitting on the fender of the tractor, the driver of the tractor was driving SCCH - 7 the said tractor and trailer in a rash and negligent manner, as a result, the deceased who was sitting on the engine or fender of the tractor fell down and the wheel of the tractor ran over the him and there is a negligence on the part of the driver of the tanker.
The driver of the tractor and trailer allowing of the deceased to sit on the engine of the tractor itself
shows the negligence on the part of the driver of the tractor which is violation of the provisions of the motor vehicle as such there are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.3 contended that as on the date of the accident the driver of Tractor and Trailer was not having valid and effective driving licence, as such it is violation of terms and Munivenkatamma vs R. Narayanaswamy on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122510435/
3 conditions of the policy as such there are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.issue:
:: I S S U E S ::
(1) Whether the Petitioners proves that deceased Sri. Narayanaswamy S/o Munidasappa sustained injuries due to the rash and negligent act of driving of Tanker bearing registration No.KA01 SCCH - 7 AL8683 dated 15.09.2021 at about 8.00 p.m., and succumbed to injuries?
(2) Whether the Petitioners proves the age and earnings of the deceased as stated in the claim petition?
(3) Whether the petitioners prove that they are legal heirs of deceased Narayanaswamy S/o Munidasappa?
(4) Whether petitioners are entitled for  compensation? If so, what is the  quantum? from whom?
 (5) What order or award?

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
At the time of the accident in front of the tanker the Tractor and Trailer was proceeding and the driver of the Tractor and Trailer at the road hump slow down his vehicle or stopped his vehicle without giving any sign or signal at that time the tanker was coming from the back side
the tractor and trailer and Tanker driver was not able to control his vehicle and dashed to the Trailer.
If the driver of the Tractor and Trailer was cautious and he was given signal or sign and slow down his vehicle at the road hump the driver of the Tanker could have control his vehicle and this accident would have avoided but from the evidence of both parties it goes to shows that the driver of the Tractor and SCCH - 7 Trailer was negligent in crossing the road hump suddenly slow down and the Tractor and Trailer without giving any sign or signal at the same time the Tanker was came from the back side of the Tractor and Trailer and the driver was driving the tanker in high speed, rash and negligent manner and he has not maintained proper distance in between his Tanker and the Tractor and Trailer and suddenly drove the same and dashed to the Tralier due to which the deceased Narayanaswamy who was sitting on the mudguard and driver of the tractor and trailer were fell down due to the force of the accident and tractor wheel ran over the head of Narayanaswamy due to which he sustained grievous injuries.
From the evidence of PW.1 it is clear that petitioner No.1 is the mother, petitioner No.2 is the wife and petitioner No.3 to 5 are the major daughters of the deceased.
By perusing the petition averments and evidence of PW.1 it is clear that all the petitioners are majors and they are having independent source of income.
In the authority reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356 in between National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Birender and Others wherein it is held that it is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased having right to apply for compensation.
Having said that it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact that whether they are fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit their claim towards conventional head only.
Hence by relying on the above said authority I am of he considered view that the petitioners are the dependents of the deceased.
Hence the petitioners No.1 to 5 are considered as dependents of the deceased.
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of consortium is Rs.2,00,000/

The respondent No.3 has admitted that as on the date of the accident the Tractor and Trailer bearing registration No.KA44T1113 and KA40T 7254 was insured by them, but the tractoir and trailer was SCCH - 7 not having FC as such it is violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.

, as such the respondent No.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
As this accident is occurred due to the negligence of the driver Tractor and Tailor bearing registration No.KA44T1113 and KA40T7254 and so also due to the negligence of the driver of the Milk Tanker bearing registration No.KA01AL8683 and the drivers of both vehicles are equally contributed for this accident and there is contributory negligence in between the drivers of the above said vehicles.
Hence I am of the considered view that the respondent No.1 being the owner Milk Tanker bearing registration No.KA01AL8683 is liable to pay 50% of the compensation amount and respondent No.2 being the owner of the Tractor and Tailor bearing registration No.KA 44T1113 and KA40T7254 and Respondent No.3 being the insurer of the said Tractor and Trailer are jointly and SCCH - 7 severally liable to pay 50% of the compensation amount to the petitioners along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition.
